name: TX-19
label: Safe R

key_factors: District's partisan lean of roughly 25 points Republican makes this one of the reddest House seats
Tom Sell has raised $2.5 million with $1.3 million in outside support versus $46,000 for Kyle Rable
Prediction markets price the Republican at about 97 percent
Open seat after Jodey Arrington's retirement, but no evidence of a competitive Democratic campaign
model.rationale: The district's 25-point Republican lean, Tom Sell's overwhelming fundraising and outside-spending advantage, and market pricing near 97 percent for the GOP leave no realistic path for Kyle Rable in this open seat.
model.watch: A late wave of Democratic outside spending or an unexpected Republican stumble could narrow the margin, though the outcome is very unlikely to be in doubt.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Jodey Arrington (R) is not on the ballot.

overview:
TX-19 is an open seat in one of the most Republican-leaning districts in the country, with a partisan lean of roughly 25 points toward the GOP. Jodey Arrington's retirement does not change the underlying arithmetic. Republican Tom Sell has raised about $2.5 million and drawn roughly $1.3 million in outside support, while Democrat Kyle Rable has raised about $46,000 with minimal cash on hand. Prediction markets give the Republican about a 97 percent chance of winning.

No public polling covers the race, so the forecast rests on district fundamentals, the fundraising gap, and market pricing. The national political environment may be somewhat favorable to Democrats, but not nearly enough to offset the district's lean in the absence of a competitive campaign. The seat is rated Safe R, with the main uncertainty being the size of the Republican margin rather than the outcome.
